title: Assessment of joint health and bleeding symptoms in women with haemophilia A and B
summary:
Hemophilia (Hemophilia A and B) is an inherited blood clotting disorder. It is inherited through the X chromosome and therefore primarily affects men. Women can pass on the mutated gene without developing severe symptoms themselves. They are called carriers. Some carriers still experience symptoms. These include very heavy menstrual bleeding, bleeding that lasts an unusually long time after injuries, and bleeding into the joints. Over time, such joint bleeding can damage the joint. To date, joint health has been studied primarily in male patients. In contrast, much less is known about affected women. More research is therefore needed to ensure that they, too, receive appropriate treatment in the future and that long-term damage can be prevented. 
The aim of this study is therefore to assess joint health and bleeding symptoms in carriers of hemophilia A and B and to evaluate their impact on pain, quality of life, and activities of daily living.
The study will include approximately 70 female carriers of hemophilia A and B who are ≤ 60 years of age and have reduced levels of clotting factors in their blood (below 50%). They will be compared with 70 women without a bleeding disorder who are of similar age and have a similar body mass index. The joint status will be assessed once by physical examination of the joints, complemented by a standardized ultrasound examination.Additionally all participants will complete questionnaires about bleeding events, joint health, daily activities, pain, and quality of life, as well as questions regarding their medical history related to menstruation and gynecology.

interventions.name: Examination of joint status and functionality in female carriers of Hemophilia A and B (FVIII/FIX < 50%): patients will be examined once by physical examination and  joint sonography. Additionally validated patient questionnaires about limitation of all-day activities, pain and healt-related quality

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- hereditary hemophilia A or B carriers
- at least two measurememts of Factor VIII or FIX < 50 %
Exclusion criteria:
- presence of other bleeding disorders
- patients with other conditions affecting the joints
- patients  incapable of giving informed consent.
